resources.string: Compare MediaCodec and JNI / NDK with a moving test pattern
Hardware video decoders only by default. libopus is software audio processing and is outside this test. The fixed sample is 640×360, 30 fps, 2 seconds. Projection settings are preserved.
For API comparison only; software success does not count as hardware success

Bring the preview into view before starting. Surface paths play a moving pattern for two seconds; buffer output only counts decoded frames. Leaving, backgrounding, or requesting a connection ends the test.
Decoded or submitted frames do not prove a visible picture. Record the last path after completion; run paths separately to judge each one. Summaries enter the existing log queue; upload is manual.

MIME creation, callbacks, input CSD, operating-rate 45 and immediate rendering. Feed at the sample arrival pace.
UCar with two QTI parameter requests. Requires an actual QTI/QCOM hardware decoder; others are skipped. Accepted keys do not prove activation.
MIME creation, priority 0, input CSD, synchronous Surface output and boolean rendering. Base calls only; business parameter maps and HiSilicon extensions are not assumed.
H.264 only. Surface color format, configured rate 33, input CSD and boolean rendering. The sample remains 30 fps; waits are bounded.
H.264 only. Surface, rate 30, low-latency 2 request and input CSD. An OEM parameter experiment; acceptance does not prove low latency.
H.264 only. No Surface: YUV buffer output, rate 30, max input 1536000 and low-latency 2 request. Counts frames/bytes without displaying or saving pixels.
